... Respondents,
PRAYER: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 
praying for the issuance of a writ of Mandamus forbearing the 5th Respondent,
his Officers and his Subordinates or any one acting through them or under them from in any manner interfering with (the petitioner) his legal right to carry on his business continuously and on his representation dated 30.11.2016.
!
For Petitioner : Mr.E.Somasundaram For Respondents : Mr.A.Muthukaruppan
Additional
Government
Pleader :ORDER

The petitioner seeks for a Mandamus forbearing the 5th respondent from in any manner interfering with the petitioner's legal right to carry on his business.
2.The petitioner is running a business in the name of Sri Vetrivelmurugan, selling small salt packets.
The grievance of the petitioner is that the fifth respondent has unlawfully interfered with his business and seized the some salt packets also by sealing the premises without following rules on 29.11.2016.
3.

A counter affidavit is filed by the fifth respondent, wherein, it is contended that the petitioner manufactured salt packets by using forged license number and therefore, the premises was inspected and samples were taken on suspicion and that the same were sent for analysis to the Principal Analysis Laboratory, Thanjavur, on 29.11.2016.
It is further stated in the counter affidavit that 14300 kg salt packets (572x25=14300) are kept in the safe custody of the Food Business Operator under.

It is further stated in the counter affidavit that the samples were analyzed and the result was received on 12.10.2016 and it was found that there is violation of certain provisions of the relevant enactment.

It is further stated that the fifth respondent sent the above Lab Report along with notice under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and rules made thereunder to the petitioner on 12.12.2016.
Thus, it is stated in the counter affidavit that the complaint is to be filed before the Adjudicating Officer under Section 68 of the above said Act for adjudication of the matter.

4.This Court, at this stage, is not inclined to go into all the rival contentions of the parties as it is for the Adjudicating Authority to consider and decide the same on merits and in accordance with law.

However, the grievance of the petitioner herein is that entire premises is locked, where, apart from the disputed salt packets, which were seized, some other household items of the petitioner are also kept inside.
Therefore, it is stated that the fifth respondent may be directed to open the premises and shift the seized salt packets to some other location.

5.The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents submitted that the fifth respondent would do so without prejudice to the proceedings already initiated against the J.Karthikeyan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 19 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4552883/
2 petitioner.
6.Considering all these aspects, this writ petition is disposed of with the following directions:-
(a) the fifth respondent shall open the premises in the presence of the petitioner,
after giving due notice to him.
(b) after opening the premises, the fifth respondent shall remove the salt packets already seized and kept in safe custody to some other premises of his choice for keeping the same under safe custody continuously.
(c) on such removal of the seized salt packets from the petitioner's premises, the petitioner shall be permitted to occupy the premises.
(d) the proceedings initiated under the abovesaid Food Safety and Standard Act,
2006 shall be completed in accordance with the procedure contemplated therein as expeditiously as possible.
